constructed: Section prose for the claim checker, constructed rather than captured until 6.6, because the model that writes a section arrives there. The three cause paragraphs arrived at 6.6, and two of them are the local model's own sentences from the first pass it wrote over this fixture, one cut to the fault it is kept for. Every figure in it was written against the facts file this fixture produces for KEYS on 2026-09-08, which is read back at test time from a replayed store rather than stated here, so a paragraph whose figures stopped matching would fail as a rejection nobody expected rather than pass as a copy of a number. Citations are written as the marker the checker reads, a D followed by the position of the document in the section's own source list, and each source is named by the fixture file or the constructed document it resolves to. From the 6.4 correction of 2026-10-09 a sentence stating the night's figures also carries [N], so the cause citing a release filed after its move, whose two figures the release does not both state, is kept for the move's span alone. From the 6.10 correction of 2026-10-10 the clean computed paragraph and the poisoned one, which stood in the key under each figure, a section no pass writes any more, stand in the segment commentary, each sentence citing [N] with the release in the source list, so the facts file alone still holds their figures. From 18.4 each paragraph states only the figures the region of the page its section sits in draws: the computed paragraphs in the segment commentary the segments' revenue and growth where they had stated the close, the averages, the margins and the multiple, the researched paragraph a segment's revenue its release states where it had stated the company's, and the causes the move's own size and no figure of the quarter, which they say in words. The clean paragraphs are here beside the rejected ones on purpose: a checker that only ever saw prose written to be refused would measure nothing about what it accepts, and what it wrongly refuses is a section left out of every report. KEYS rather than AAPL, and the reason is a property of the replay: its corporate action check refetches AAPL's year as of the action's own session, so AAPL's stored series ends on 2026-08-10 and the replay writes no facts file for it on the fixture night at all. KEYS is refetched by nothing and holds the same facts file in every chain the suite replays.

sections.name: a clean computed paragraph
sections.prose: Communications Solutions Group revenue for the quarter ended 2026-07-31 was $1,345 million, up 43.1% on a year earlier [N]. Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue was $501 million, up 21.6% [N]. Revenue across the two segments was $1,846 million, up 36.5% [N].
sections.carries: every figure a rounding of one the facts file holds for the segments, which the segment commentary's region draws, at the precision the prose itself states: $1,345 million of 1345000000, 43.1% of a growth stored as the fraction 0.430851, 21.6% of 0.216019 and 36.5% of the two segments' growth 0.365385. One date, the quarter's end. Every sentence cites the night's stored figures by [N] and no document, so each figure is held to the facts file alone; the release stands in the source list because a section whose list holds no admitted document is not read at all.

sections.name: a poisoned paragraph
sections.prose: Communications Solutions Group revenue for the quarter ended 2026-07-31 was $1,345 million, up 43.6% on a year earlier [N]. Electronic Industrial Solutions Group revenue was $501 million, up 21.6% [N]. Revenue across the two segments was $1,846 million, up 36.5% [N].
sections.carries: the clean paragraph above with one figure changed, a growth of 43.6% where the facts file holds 0.430851. A near miss rather than an absurd figure, half a point from the true growth, because the wrong figure a writer produces is a slip of rounding far more often than an invention, and a poison further away would be refused by a checker that had stopped reading the precision the prose states. One and only one, so the rejection is asserted to name exactly that figure rather than to have found something wrong somewhere in a paragraph of seven.

sections.name: a clean researched paragraph
sections.prose: Keysight sells electronic design and test instruments, software and services to communications, aerospace, defence and semiconductor customers [D1]. Communications Solutions Group revenue for the July quarter was $1,345 million [D1].
sections.carries: a citation on every sentence, resolving to the release exhibit the filings archive holds, which is admitted, and one figure the release states that is also in the facts file for the segments, which the section's region draws. A claim resting on a document has to name it and a figure in it has to be one code computed, and this paragraph satisfies both halves so neither can be what the rejections below turn on.

sections.name: an unsourced claim
sections.prose: Keysight sells electronic design and test instruments, software and services to communications, aerospace, defence and semiconductor customers [D1]. Analysts expect the next design cycle to be the strongest in five years.
sections.carries: the same first sentence and a second that names no document at all. It carries no digit, so the number rule has nothing to say about it and the citation rule is the only thing that can refuse it, which is the shape of a confident wrong sentence the decision is about.

sections.name: a claim resting on a refused document
sections.prose: Keysight sells electronic design and test instruments, software and services to communications, aerospace, defence and semiconductor customers [D1]. Its test business is expected to keep growing faster than its software [D2].
sections.carries: a citation that resolves to a stored row admissibility refused. The document is stored, so a rule asking only whether a source exists would pass it, and the claim checker reads the verdict on the row rather than applying the test again, which 6.0 ruled.

sections.name: a section with no admissible source
sources: inadmissible: a page with no publish date
sections.carries: a section whose whole source list was refused, which is what a pass leaves when it fetched documents and admitted none of them. It goes to fallback on the first check rather than being given a retry, because a rewrite cannot create a source, and what the name page draws for it is one line saying no admissible source was found.

sections.name: a cause citing a release filed after the move
sections.section: The cause of each large move
sections.prose: The largest move, of 28.62 per cent, ended on 2026-02-24 and was driven by the company reporting record third quarter revenue [D1] [N].
sections.carries: the first draft a local model wrote for this section at 6.6, with the one date it quoted that the facts file does not hold taken out and, from 18.4, the quarter's revenue said in words, so that only the rule this paragraph is for can refuse it. Every figure is a rounding of a fact and the citation resolves to an admitted document, which is everything the checker asked of a sentence before 6.6. What it states is false: the release was filed on 2026-08-18 and the move it is cited for was measured from 2026-02-17 to 2026-02-24.

sections.name: a cause naming no move
sections.section: The cause of each large move
sections.prose: Keysight shares moved on record third quarter revenue [D1].
sections.carries: a cause with a citation that names no stored move's session, so nothing says which move it is about and no span exists to hold its document against.

sections.name: a cause of the move the release falls inside
sections.section: The cause of each large move
sections.prose: The move from 2026-08-17 to 2026-08-24 was driven by record third quarter results, with revenue and GAAP net income both at records, as detailed in the results release exhibit [D1].
sections.carries: the sentence the local model wrote on its first draft once the writer handed it the one move the release falls inside, captured at 6.6 and accepted, its quarter's two figures said in words from 18.4 since the latest quarter draws them: the release was filed on 2026-08-18, inside the move measured from 2026-08-17 and ended on 2026-08-24. Accepted is not the same as true, and this paragraph carries that too: the checker holds when the document was published and every figure in the sentence, and not that a company's own release says why its shares fell.

attempts.name: rejected twice
attempts.carries: the retry bound. The second attempt fails as the first did, so the section goes to fallback with both attempts' offending text kept, the first on its own rejected row and the second on the fallback row, and no third attempt is checked as a retry of either.

attempts.name: rejected then accepted
attempts.carries: the retry doing what it is for, so the bound is not asserted over a checker that simply refuses every second attempt.
